messages:
maria: Heads up — prod-gpu-v2 in us-west-2 has sustained queue growth for ~10m, 500s spiking. P95 latency creeping up. Can we do a targeted spillover instead of full cross-region failover? Unsure of cost hit.
kevin: +1 to targeted. First cheap win: deprioritize warm pools and soft-evict low-priority requests. Warm pools are eating slots under heavy prefix-KV churn.
sophie: We should avoid spilling premium traffic across regions. Proposal: admission control rule — when queue_depth_per_pool > 180, only spill tier=standard to eu-west-1 and apply model-fallback to redwood-opt-6.7b-int8. Keep tier=premium pinned to same-region.
oliver: Example routing snippet — canary it for 2m:
```yaml
routing_rules:
  - name: spill-standard-on-saturation
    trigger:
      queue_depth: ">180"
    action:
      - route: eu-west-1:pool=prod-gpu-v2-small
        selectors: ["tier:standard"]
      - fallback_model: redwood-opt-6.7b-int8
      - deprioritize_pools: [warm-pool-1,warm-pool-2]
    canary: 2m
    rate_limit: 0.15  # fraction of standard traffic to spill
```
kevin: Also add a short per-tenant admission window: if tenant_queue_time > 4s then reject/queue with 429 and suggest client-side retry with jitter. That prevents a single noisy-tenant from hogging spill budget.
capacity-bot: current_metrics: capacity_signal=0.12; available_slots=18; avg_queue_depth=235; tail_latency_p95=460ms; affected_pools=[prod-gpu-v2(us-west-2)].
sophie: With available_slots that low, full spillover will cost a lot and increase end-to-end latency for EU users. So prefer model-fallback + deprioritize warm pools + per-tenant shed first.
maria: Can we simulate cost delta? If spill 20% of standard traffic to eu-west-1 it will add ~+22% GPU-hour egress/ops margin from quick calc. Want to minimize.
kevin: Agree — fallback to smaller quantized model for spill path reduces token-cost and GPU time. Also enable KV prefix cache for repeated prompts to lower per-token compute on spill targets.
oliver: I'll run the canary. Applying routing change with the deploy tool now: `deployctl apply routing spill-standard-on-saturation --canary 2m --env prod`
deploy-bot: routing change applied, canary started for spill-standard-on-saturation. Monitoring channels: #observability and #incidents.
sophie: I'll add a temporary alert: if spill_rate > 0.25 && avg_queue_depth > 200 -> page infra-oncall. Also will add a note to runbook: prefer model-fallback before cross-region for cost-sensitive customers. Link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/fleet-saturation (draft) :memo:
maria: Perfect. If canary looks good, let's keep deprioritize_warm_pools enabled and escalate to 10% -> 50% spill in controlled increments. Keep premium pinned.
kevin: One more: log a metric 'spill_decision_reason' with values {queue_based,warmpool_evict,tenant_shed} so we can analyze which lever triggered spill.
maria: Thanks — looping in eng-sre if we see paging. Will post results in ~10m. :eyes:
